title.zh: 卷一百四十 列傳第六十五 崔苗二裴呂
title.en: Volume 140 Biographies 65: Cui Miao, two Pei's, Lu
title.raw: 卷一百四十 列傳第六十五 崔苗二裴呂 Volume 140 Biographies 65: Cui Miao, two Pei's, Lu

sentences.zh: 崔苗二裴呂

translations.literal: Cui, Miao, two Pei's, Lu
translations.idiomatic: Cui, Miao, the two Peis, and Lu

translations.literal: 4.1.1 Pei Shu
translations.idiomatic: 4.1.1 Pei Shu

sentences.zh: 崔圓，字有裕，貝州武城人，後魏尚書左仆射亮八世孫。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan, styled Youyu, was a man of Wucheng in Beizhou, eighth-generation descendant of Cui Liang, Vice Director of the Left Department of the Secretariat of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan, styled Youyu, came from Wucheng in Beizhou and was the eighth-generation descendant of Cui Liang, who had served as Vice Director of the Left Department of the Secretariat under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，志向卓邁，喜學兵家。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, his ambitions were lofty, and he delighted in studying military treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth and raised in poverty, he harbored lofty ambitions and took pleasure in studying the military classics.

sentences.zh: 開元中，詔舉遺逸，以鈐謀對策甲科，歷京兆府參軍，尹蕭炅薦之，遷會昌丞。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era an edict summoned men of outstanding talent neglected by office; he answered the policy examination on military strategy in the top grade, successively served as an aide in the metropolitan prefecture, was recommended by Prefect Xiao Jiong, and was promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign an edict called up neglected men of talent; Yuan passed the policy examination on military strategy at the top grade, served as an aide in the capital prefecture, won recommendation from Prefect Xiao Jiong, and was promoted to assistant magistrate of Huichang.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠遙領劍南節度，引圓為左司馬，知留後。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong held the Sword River circuit commandery in absentia and brought Yuan in as Left Chief Military Administrator with charge of the rear command.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong held the Sword River commandery in absentia and brought Yuan in as left chief military administrator with charge of the rear headquarters.

sentences.zh: 玄宗西出，次撫風，遷御史中丞、劍南節度副大使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong marched west and halted at Fufeng, Yuan was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and deputy military commissioner of the Sword River circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong marched west and halted at Fufeng, Yuan was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and deputy military commissioner of the Sword River circuit.

sentences.zh: 圓銳功名，初聞難，刺國忠意，乃治城浚隍，列館宇，儲什具。

translations.literal: Yuan was keen for merit and fame; at first news of the turmoil, discerning Yang Guozhong's intent, he fortified the city, deepened the moat, arrayed lodges, and stored supplies and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious for merit and fame, Yuan took the first news of rebellion as a cue to Yang Guozhong's intentions: he fortified the city, deepened the moat, set up lodges, and stockpiled provisions and equipment.

sentences.zh: 帝次河池，圓疏具陳「蜀土腴穀羨，儲供易辦」。

translations.literal: When the Emperor stopped at Hechi, Yuan submitted a memorial fully stating that "the land of Shu is fertile and grain abundant; storage and supply are easy to arrange."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor halted at Hechi, Yuan submitted a detailed memorial arguing that "the soil of Shu is rich and grain plentiful—stores and supplies are easy to prepare."

sentences.zh: 帝省書泣下曰：「世亂識忠臣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor read the letter, wept, and said: "In chaotic times one recognizes loyal ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial, wept, and said, "In troubled times one learns who the loyal ministers are."

sentences.zh: 即日拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，仍兼劍南節度使。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and still concurrent military commissioner of the Sword River circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Yuan was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, grand councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, while retaining his post as military commissioner of the Sword River circuit.

sentences.zh: 天子至，朝廷百司殿宇帷幔皆具，益嗟賞之。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven arrived, the hundred offices of the court—halls, curtains, and all—were ready; he admired this all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven arrived, the halls, curtains, and furnishings of every court office were already in place, and his admiration for Yuan only grew.

sentences.zh: 肅宗立，命與房琯、韋見素赴行在所，帝為製遺愛碑於蜀以寵之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong was established, he was ordered to go with Fang Guan and Wei Jiansu to the mobile court; the Emperor had an "Inscribed Stele of Enduring Favor" made in Shu to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Suzong took the throne, Yuan was ordered to join Fang Guan and Wei Jiansu at the mobile court; the emperor had a stele of enduring favor carved in Shu to honor him.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，遷中書令，封趙國公，實封戶五百。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with five hundred households of actual fief revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhide era he was promoted to director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with five hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，罷為太子少師，留守東都。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan he was dismissed to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and remained to guard the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan he was removed from office, made grand mentor of the heir apparent, and left to guard the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 於是上皇所置宰相無在者。

translations.literal: Thus among the chancellors the Retired Emperor had appointed, none remained.
translations.idiomatic: At that point none of the chancellors the retired emperor had appointed still held office.

sentences.zh: 王師之敗相州也，軍所過，皆縱剽，圓懼，委東都，奔襄陽，詔削階、封。

translations.literal: When the royal army was defeated at Xiangzhou, wherever the troops passed they were allowed to plunder freely; Yuan was afraid, abandoned the Eastern Capital, fled to Xiangyang, and an edict stripped his rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial army's defeat at Xiangzhou, the troops were allowed to loot wherever they marched; frightened, Yuan abandoned the Eastern Capital and fled to Xiangyang, and an edict stripped his rank and enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 尋召拜濟王傅。

translations.literal: Soon after he was recalled and appointed Tutor of the Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and appointed tutor to the Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 李光弼表為懷州刺史，改汾州，以治行稱。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi memorialized that he be made Prefect of Huaizhou; he was transferred to Fenzhou, renowned for his governing conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi recommended him as prefect of Huaizhou; he was later transferred to Fenzhou, where his administrative record won praise.

sentences.zh: 徙淮南節度使，在鎮六年，請朝京師，吏民乞留，詔檢校尚書右仆射，還之。

translations.literal: He was moved to military commissioner of Huainan; after six years in the circuit he requested to attend court in the capital; officials and commoners begged that he stay; an edict made him acting Minister of the Right and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of Huainan; after six years in the circuit he asked to attend court in the capital, but officials and commoners begged him to stay, so an edict made him acting minister of the right and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 久乃檢校左仆射，入知省事。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made acting Minister of the Left and entered to handle matters in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval was he made acting minister of the left and entered the Secretariat to handle its business.

sentences.zh: 大歷中卒，年六十四，贈太子太師，謚曰昭襄。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he died at sixty-four, was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and given the posthumous title Zhaoxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Dali era at sixty-four, was posthumously made grand preceptor of the heir apparent, and received the posthumous title Zhaoxiang.

sentences.zh: 苗晉卿

translations.literal: Miao Jinqing
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jinqing

sentences.zh: 苗晉卿，字元輔，潞州壺關人，世以儒素稱。

translations.literal: Miao Jinqing, styled Yuanfu, was a native of Huguan in Luzhou; his family was renowned for plain Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jinqing, styled Yuanfu, was a native of Huguan in Luzhou; his family had long been known for plain Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，調為修武尉，累進吏部郎中、中書舍人，知吏部選事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Xiuwu, and was successively promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Secretariat Drafter, and put in charge of personnel selection in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Xiuwu, and rose through the posts of director in the Ministry of Personnel and secretariat drafter until he was put in charge of personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 選人訴索好官，厲言倨色紛於前，晉卿與相對，終日無慍顏。

translations.literal: Candidates lodging complaints and demanding good posts pressed toward him with stern words and arrogant expressions; Jinqing faced them across the table all day long without a trace of anger on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who came to complain and demand better posts pressed him with harsh words and arrogant faces; Jinqing sat opposite them all day without a trace of anger.

sentences.zh: 久之，進侍郎，積寬縱，而吏下因緣作奸。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Vice Minister, accumulated lax indulgence, and subordinate clerks took opportunity to commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was promoted to vice minister; laxness accumulated, and subordinate clerks seized the opening to commit fraud.

sentences.zh: 方時承平，選常萬人，李林甫為尚書，專國政，以銓事委晉卿及宋遙，然歲命它官同較書判，核才實。

translations.literal: At a time of general peace, selections often ran to ten thousand men; Li Linfu was Minister and monopolized state affairs, entrusting examination affairs to Jinqing and Song Yao—yet each year other officials were ordered to join in reviewing documents and passes to verify true talent.
translations.idiomatic: In those peaceful years selections often involved ten thousand men; Li Linfu, as minister, monopolized state affairs and entrusted the examination process to Jinqing and Song Yao, yet each year other officials were ordered to join in reviewing papers and passes to verify true ability.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年，判入等者凡六十四人，分甲、乙、丙三科，以張奭為第一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao, those judged to have entered the ranks totaled sixty-four persons, divided into three classes—A, B, and C—with Zhang Shi ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianbao, sixty-four candidates were judged to have passed, divided into three grades—A, B, and C—with Zhang Shi placed first.

sentences.zh: 奭，御史中丞倚之子，倚新得幸於帝，晉卿欲附之，奭本無學，故議者囂然不平。

translations.literal: Shi was the son of Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi; Yi had newly won the Emperor's favor; Jinqing wished to attach himself to him; Shi was fundamentally without learning—hence critics clamored in outrage.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was the son of censor-in-chief Zhang Yi, who had newly won the emperor's favor; Jinqing wished to curry favor with him, but Shi was utterly without learning, and critics erupted in outrage.

sentences.zh: 安祿山因間言之，帝為禦花萼樓覆實，中裁十一二，奭持紙終日，筆不下，人謂之「曳白」。

translations.literal: An Lushan seized on the opening to speak of it; the Emperor held a verification at the Hua'e Tower; more than nine-tenths failed; Shi held his sheet all day without the brush descending—people called it "dragging the white."
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan seized the chance to bring it up; the emperor held a verification at the Hua'e Tower, and more than nine-tenths failed; Shi held his examination paper all day without setting brush to paper—people called it "dragging the blank."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，貶倚淮陽太守，遙武當太守，晉卿安康太守。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and demoted Yi to prefect of Huaiyang, Yao to prefect of Wudang, and Jinqing to prefect of Ankang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and demoted Yi to prefect of Huaiyang, Yao to prefect of Wudang, and Jinqing to prefect of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙魏郡，即充河北采訪使。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Weijun and appointed concurrently Regional Inspector of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Weijun and appointed regional inspector of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 居三年，政化大行。

translations.literal: After three years in office, government and transformation flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office, his policies had taken deep root throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 嘗入計，謁歸壺關，望縣門輒步，吏諫止，晉卿以「公門當下，況父母邦乎」？

translations.literal: Once when entering to render accounts he returned to visit Huguan; when he saw the county gate he would walk; clerks remonstrated and stopped him, but Jinqing said, "At the public gate one must dismount—how much more in one's parents' homeland!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, on returning from the capital to present accounts, he visited Huguan; whenever he saw the county gate he would dismount and walk; clerks urged him to stop, but Jinqing said, "One dismounts at the public gate—how much more in one's native home!"

sentences.zh: 郡太守迎犒，使所屬令行酒，酒至，必立飲白釂，侍老有獻，降西階拜而飲，時美其恭。

translations.literal: When the commandery prefect came out to welcome and entertain him, he had subordinate magistrates pass the wine; whenever wine arrived he would always rise and drain a full cup; when elders of the district presented offerings he would descend the western steps, bow, and drink—contemporaries praised his respectfulness.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery prefect came out to welcome and feast him, he had the subordinate magistrates pass the wine; whenever a cup arrived he would rise and drain it to the dregs; when village elders offered wine he would descend the western steps, bow, and drink—contemporaries praised his reverence.

sentences.zh: 改河東郡，兼河東采訪使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hedong commandery and concurrently made Regional Inspector of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hedong commandery and made concurrent regional inspector of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 徙撫風郡，封高平縣男。

translations.literal: He was moved to Fufeng commandery and enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Fufeng commandery and enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書、東都留守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Works and Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of works and defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 召為憲部，兼左丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the Ministry of Justice and concurrently made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the Ministry of Justice and made concurrent left vice director.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，竇廷芝棄陜郡不守，楊國忠本忌其有望，即奏「東道賊沖，非大臣不可鎮遏」，授陜郡太守、陜虢防禦使，晉卿見帝，以老辭，忤旨，聽致仕於家。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Dou Tingzhi abandoned Shaan commandery without holding it; Yang Guozhong had long resented Jinqing's popular standing and immediately memorialized: "The eastern road is where bandits will strike; only a great minister can suppress them," appointing him Prefect of Shaan commandery and Defense Commissioner of Shan-Guo; when Jinqing saw the Emperor he pleaded old age in refusal, contravened the imperial intent, and was permitted to retire at home.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Dou Tingzhi abandoned Shaan commandery without defending it; Yang Guozhong, who had long resented Jinqing's standing with the people, immediately memorialized that "the eastern route is where the rebels will strike—only a great minister can hold them back," and appointed him prefect of Shaan commandery and defense commissioner of Shan-Guo; when Jinqing saw the emperor he pleaded old age and declined, contravened the imperial will, and was permitted to retire at home.

sentences.zh: 車駕入蜀，搢紳多陷賊，晉卿間道走金州。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage entered Shu, gentry and officials mostly fell into the rebels' hands; Jinqing took bypaths and fled to Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage entered Shu, most of the gentry and officials fell into rebel hands; Jinqing took hidden routes and fled to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉卿寬厚，所至以惠化稱。

translations.literal: Jinqing was generous and mild; wherever he went he was known for benevolent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was generous and mild; wherever he served he was known for benevolent government.

sentences.zh: 魏人為營生祠，立石頌美。

translations.literal: The people of Wei built a living shrine for him and set up a stone praising his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei built a living shrine to him and erected a stone praising his virtues.

sentences.zh: 再秉政，出入七年，小心謹畏，不甚斥是非得失，故能安保寵名。

translations.literal: Holding power a second time, coming and going for seven years, he was cautious and timid and did not much criticize others' rights and wrongs, gains and losses—thus he could safely preserve favor and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as chief minister a second time for seven years in all, he was cautious and restrained and rarely denounced others' rights and wrongs or gains and losses—thus he was able to preserve favor and reputation in safety.

sentences.zh: 然練達事體，百官簿最，一省無遺，議者比漢胡廣。

translations.literal: Yet he was thoroughly versed in institutional matters; the ledgers of the hundred offices—he could recall all in one consultation without omission; critics compared him to Hu Guang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was thoroughly versed in the workings of government; the ledgers of the hundred offices—he could survey them all at a glance without omission—and critics compared him to Hu Guang of Han.

sentences.zh: 肅宗欲以李輔國為常侍，奏曰：「常侍近密，非賢不可居，豈宜任等輩？」

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong wished to make Li Fuguo a palace attendant; Jinqing memorialized: "The palace attendant's post is intimate and close; no one but the worthy should hold it—how can someone of that sort be appointed?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong wished to make Li Fuguo a palace attendant, Jinqing memorialized: "The palace attendant's post is intimate and close; only the worthy should hold it—how can someone of that sort be appointed?"

sentences.zh: 罷之。

translations.literal: The appointment was cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was cancelled.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲論陳希烈等死，晉卿曰：「陛下得張通儒、安守忠、孫孝哲等，何以加罪？」

translations.literal: When the court wished to debate putting Chen Xilie and others to death, Jinqing said: "Your Majesty has already obtained Zhang Tongru, An Shouzhong, Sun Xiaozhe, and the rest—how can you add further punishment?"
translations.idiomatic: When the court wished to debate putting Chen Xilie and others to death, Jinqing said, "Your Majesty has already obtained Zhang Tongru, An Shouzhong, Sun Xiaozhe, and the rest—how can you add further punishment?"

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 俄而史思明亂，持是以誘眾。

translations.literal: Before long Shi Siming rebelled and used this as bait to win followers.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shi Siming rebelled and used this episode to win followers.

sentences.zh: 嘗自為父碑文，有鵲巢碑上。

translations.literal: He once wrote an epitaph for his father himself; magpies nested on the stele.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed an epitaph for his father himself; magpies nested on the stele.

sentences.zh: 賊入上黨，焚蕩略盡，而苗氏松槚獨無傷。

translations.literal: When bandits entered Shangdang they burned and ravaged nearly everything, yet the Miao clan's pine and cypress groves alone were unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels entered Shangdang they burned and ravaged nearly everything, yet the Miao clan's pine and cypress groves alone were left untouched.

sentences.zh: 大歷七年，配享肅宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali he was enshrined for joint sacrifice in the temple court of Emperor Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dali he was granted joint sacrifice in the temple court of Emperor Suzong.

sentences.zh: 十子：發、丕、堅、粲、垂、向、呂、稷、望、咸。

translations.literal: Ten sons: Fa, Pi, Jian, Can, Chui, Xiang, Lü, Ji, Wang, Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons: Fa, Pi, Jian, Can, Chui, Xiang, Lü, Ji, Wang, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 粲，德宗時官至郎中，陸贄欲進粲官，帝不許，曰：「晉卿往攝政，有不臣之言。

translations.literal: Can, in Emperor Dezong's time reached the office of Director; Lu Zhi wished to advance Can's office—the Emperor did not permit it and said: "When Jinqing served as regent he had words of disloyalty to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Can, under Emperor Dezong, reached the office of director; Lu Zhi wished to promote him, but the emperor refused, saying, "When Jinqing served as regent he uttered words of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 又名其子，皆與帝王同，粲等宜與外官。」

translations.literal: Moreover he named his sons all the same as emperors; Can and the others should only receive outer-circuit posts."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he named his sons with the same names as emperors; Can and his brothers should receive only posts outside the capital."

sentences.zh: 贄奏：「王者爵人必於朝，刑人必於市，言與眾共之。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized: "The king who ennobles a man must do so in court; who punishes must do so in the market—meaning the matter is shared with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized: "A king who ennobles a man must do so in court; who punishes must do so in the market—meaning the matter is shared with the multitude.

sentences.zh: 獎而不言其善，斯謂曲貸；

translations.literal: To reward without stating the good is called crooked favor;
translations.idiomatic: To reward without stating what is good is called crooked favor;

sentences.zh: 罰而不書其惡，斯謂中傷。

translations.literal: to punish without recording the evil is called slanderous injury.
translations.idiomatic: to punish without recording what is evil is called slanderous injury.

sentences.zh: 曲貸，則授受不明，而私幸之門啟；

translations.literal: Crooked favor, then grant and acceptance are unclear, and the gate of private favor opens;
translations.idiomatic: Crooked favor leaves grant and acceptance unclear and opens the gate to private favor;

sentences.zh: 中傷，則枉直無辨，而讒間之道行。

translations.literal: slanderous injury, then crooked and straight are undistinguished, and the way of calumny and estrangement proceeds.
translations.idiomatic: slanderous injury leaves right and wrong undistinguished and lets the way of calumny prevail.

sentences.zh: 可不慎哉！

translations.literal: Can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Can one not be cautious in this!

sentences.zh: 若陛下以晉卿奸邪，粲等應坐，則當公議其罪；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty holds Jinqing treacherous and evil and Can and the others should be punished, then the crime should be debated in public;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty holds Jinqing treacherous and evil and Can and his brothers deserve punishment, then their crime should be debated in public;

sentences.zh: 若知見誣，亦宜擢粲等以示天下。

translations.literal: if you know he was slandered, you should also promote Can and the others to show the realm.
translations.idiomatic: if you know he was slandered, you should also promote Can and his brothers to show the realm.

sentences.zh: 且晉卿起文儒，致位臺輔，謙柔敦厚，為三朝所推，安肯為族滅計？

translations.literal: Moreover Jinqing rose from literary Confucianism to reach the highest offices, was humble, gentle, and sincere, and was commended by three reigns—how would he consent to a plan that would exterminate his clan?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Jinqing rose from the ranks of literary scholars to the highest offices; humble, gentle, and sincere, he was esteemed through three reigns—how would he ever consent to a plan that would destroy his entire clan?

sentences.zh: 雖甚狂險猶不為之，況老臣乎？」

translations.literal: Even the most wildly reckless would not do this—how much less an old minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Even the wildest and most reckless would not do such a thing—how much less an old minister?"

sentences.zh: 帝然之，而粲官終不顯。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed, yet Can's office never became prominent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, yet Can's career never rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 裴冕，字章甫，河中河東人，本冠族仕家，以蔭再調渭南尉。

translations.literal: Pei Mian, styled Zhangfu, was a native of Hedong in Hezhong; his family was originally of eminent clan and official household; through yin privilege he was twice appointed magistrate of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian, styled Zhangfu, came from Hedong in Hezhong; his family was of eminent official lineage, and through yin privilege he was twice appointed magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 王鉷為京畿采訪使，表署判官，歷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Wang Hong was Regional Inspector of the Capital Region; Mian was entered on his staff as aide and passed through the post of Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hong served as regional inspector of the capital region, Mian was entered on his staff as aide and later served as palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 冕少學術，然明銳，果於事，眾呈稱職，鉷雅任之。

translations.literal: Mian studied the arts from youth, yet was sharp and keen, decisive in affairs; the multitude presented him as competent in office, and Hong greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Mian had studied the classics from youth, yet he was sharp and keen and decisive in affairs; everyone regarded him as competent in office, and Hong relied on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 及鉷得罪，有詔廷辨，冕位甚下，而抗言其誣。

translations.literal: When Hong fell into guilt there was an edict for court debate; Mian's rank was very low, yet he spoke out against the false charges.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong fell from favor an edict ordered a court debate; though Mian's rank was very low, he spoke out against the false charges.

sentences.zh: 鉷死，李林甫方用事，僚屬懼，皆引去，獨冕為斂葬，由是浸知名。

translations.literal: When Hong died, Li Linfu was just then in power; staff members were afraid and all withdrew; Mian alone arranged the burial—thereby he gradually became known.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong died, Li Linfu had just come to power; his staff were afraid and all withdrew, but Mian alone arranged the burial—thereby he gradually made a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使哥舒翰辟行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Geshu Han, military commissioner of Hexi, recruited him as campaigning chief military administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, military commissioner of Hexi, recruited him as campaigning chief military administrator.

sentences.zh: 玄宗入蜀，詔皇太子為天下兵馬元帥，拜冕御史中丞兼左庶子副之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong entered Shu, an edict made the Crown Prince commander-in-chief of all armies under Heaven; Mian was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong entered Shu, an edict made the crown prince commander-in-chief of all armies; Mian was appointed vice censor-in-chief and concurrent left subordinate of the heir apparent to assist him.

sentences.zh: 初，冕在河西，方召還，而道遇太子平涼，遂從至靈武，與杜鴻漸、崔漪同辭進曰：「主上厭於勤，且南狩蜀，宗社神器，要須有歸。

translations.literal: At first Mian was in Hexi and had just been summoned back when on the road he met the Crown Prince at Pingliang; he followed on to Lingwu and, with Du Hongjian and Cui Yi, together advanced words saying: "The sovereign is weary of toil and is moreover hunting south in Shu; the altars of state and the sacred regalia must find a home.
translations.idiomatic: Mian had been in Hexi and was just being recalled when on the road he met the crown prince at Pingliang; he followed on to Lingwu and, with Du Hongjian and Cui Yi, jointly urged him: "The sovereign is weary of rule and has gone south to hunt in Shu; the altars of state and the sacred regalia must find a home.

sentences.zh: 今天意人事，屬在殿下，宜正位號。

translations.literal: Today Heaven's intent and human affairs belong to Your Highness; you should rectify the title and designation.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent and the affairs of men now rest with Your Highness; you should take the throne.

sentences.zh: 有如逡巡，失億兆心，則大事去矣。」

translations.literal: If you hesitate and lose the hearts of the myriad masses, then the great affair is lost."
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate and lose the hearts of the myriad people, the great enterprise will be lost."

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「我平寇逆，奉迎乘輿還京師，退居涼貳，以侍膳左右，豈不樂哉！

translations.literal: The Crown Prince said: "I will pacify the rebels, welcome the imperial carriage back to the capital, withdraw to a cool second place, and attend meals at the sovereign's side—how would that not be joy!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "I shall pacify the rebels, welcome the imperial carriage back to the capital, withdraw to a secondary place, and attend the sovereign at table—would that not be joy enough!

sentences.zh: 公等何言之過！」

translations.literal: How excessive are your words!"
translations.idiomatic: Why do you speak so extravagantly!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「殿下居東宮二十年，今多難啟聖，以安社稷，而所從將士皆關輔人，日夜思歸，大眾一騷，不可復集，不如因而撫之，以就大功。

translations.literal: They replied: "Your Highness has dwelt in the Eastern Palace twenty years; now in many difficulties you should inaugurate sagely rule to settle the altars of state—yet the generals and soldiers who follow you are all men of the Guan region and the capital approaches; day and night they think of returning home; if the great host is once stirred, it cannot be gathered again—better to take this occasion to reassure them and thereby accomplish the great merit.
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Your Highness has dwelt in the Eastern Palace twenty years; now in these many troubles you should inaugurate sagely rule to settle the altars of state—yet the generals and soldiers who follow you are all men of the Guan region and the capital approaches; day and night they long for home; if the great host is once stirred, it cannot be gathered again—better to reassure them now and thereby accomplish the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 臣等昧死請。」

translations.literal: We your ministers beg at the risk of death."
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers beg this at the risk of our lives."

sentences.zh: 太子固讓，凡五請，卒見聽。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince firmly declined; in all he was asked five times and finally was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince firmly declined; they urged him five times in all before he finally assented.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，進冕中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince took the throne, Mian was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince took the throne, Mian was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and grand councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 乃建言賣官、度僧道士，收貲濟軍興。

translations.literal: He then proposed selling offices and ordaining monks and Daoist priests, collecting fees to aid military mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed selling offices and ordaining monks and Daoist priests, collecting fees to fund the war effort.

sentences.zh: 時取償既賤，眾不為宜。

translations.literal: At the time the compensation taken was already cheap; the multitude did not regard it as fitting.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the fees demanded were already low, and many regarded the policy as improper.

sentences.zh: 肅宗至鳳翔，罷冕政事，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong reached Fengxiang, Mian was removed from state affairs and appointed Minister of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong reached Fengxiang, Mian was removed from state affairs and appointed minister of the right.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，封冀國公，實封五百戶，出為劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with five hundred households of actual fief revenue and sent out as military commissioner of Sword River West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were recovered, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with five hundred taxable households and sent out as military commissioner of the Sword River West circuit.

sentences.zh: 復為右僕射，待制集賢院。

translations.literal: He was again made Minister of the Right and awaited orders at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made minister of the right and served as awaiting-orders scholar at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 俄充山陵使。

translations.literal: Before long he was made commissioner for the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed commissioner for the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 於是，中書舍人劉烜為李輔國所昵，冕表為判官。

translations.literal: At this time Secretariat Drafter Liu Xuan was favored by Li Fuguo; Mian memorialized that he be made aide.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the secretariat drafter Liu Xuan was favored by Li Fuguo; Mian memorialized that he be made his aide.

sentences.zh: 烜抵法，坐降施州刺史，徙澧州。

translations.literal: Xuan violated the law and, on that account, was demoted to prefect of Shizhou and moved to Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan violated the law and was demoted to prefect of Shizhou, then transferred to Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，郭子儀言於代宗曰：「冕首佐先帝，馳驅靈武，有社稷勛，程元振忌其賢，遂加誣構，海內冤之。

translations.literal: In the Dali era Guo Ziyi spoke to Emperor Daizong saying: "Mian was the first to assist the late emperor, galloping to Lingwu; he had merit for the altars of state; Cheng Yuanzhen resented his talent and therefore added false framing—the realm was wronged on his account.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era Guo Ziyi said to Emperor Daizong, "Mian was the first to assist the late emperor, galloping to Lingwu; he earned merit for the altars of state; Cheng Yuanzhen resented his talent and framed him with false charges—the realm was wronged on his account.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜還冕於朝，復俾輔相，必能致治成化。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should return Mian to court and again make him assist as chancellor—he will surely be able to bring orderly rule and accomplished transformation."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should recall Mian to court and again make him chancellor—he will surely bring orderly rule and accomplished transformation."

sentences.zh: 時元載秉政，冕早所甄引，載德之，又貪其衰瘵，且下己，遂拜左僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zai held state affairs; Mian had long ago been selected and promoted by him; Zai was grateful to him and also coveted his feeble illness—and moreover humbled himself—so Mian was appointed Minister of the Left and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zai held power; Mian had long ago been selected and promoted by him; Zai was grateful and also took advantage of his feeble illness—and moreover humbled himself before Zai—so Mian was appointed minister of the left and grand councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 入見，拜不能興，載自扶之，代為贊謝。

translations.literal: On entering audience he could not rise in bowing; Zai himself supported him and spoke thanks in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered audience he could not rise to bow; Zai himself supported him and spoke the words of thanks in his stead.

sentences.zh: 俄兼河南江淮副元帥、東都留守。

translations.literal: Before long he was concurrently made deputy commander-in-chief of Henan and the Jiang-Huai region and Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was concurrently made deputy commander-in-chief of Henan and the Jiang-Huai region and defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 不逾月卒，有詔贈太尉。

translations.literal: In less than a month he died; an edict posthumously made him Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month he died; an edict posthumously made him grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 冕以忠勤自將，然不知宰相大體。

translations.literal: Mian conducted himself with loyalty and diligence, yet did not understand the great principles of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Mian conducted himself with loyalty and diligence, yet did not understand the great principles of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 性豪侈，既素貴，輿服食飲皆光麗珍豐，櫪馬直數百金者常十數，每廣會賓客，不能名其饌，自製巾子工甚，人爭效之，號「僕射巾」。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant; since he had long been noble, his carriages, food, clothing, and drink were all lustrous, splendid, precious, and abundant; stable horses worth several hundred cash each numbered a dozen or more at all times; whenever he held a grand gathering of guests he could not name the dishes; the headcloth he made himself was very finely crafted—people competed to imitate it, calling it the "Minister's Headcloth."
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant; long accustomed to high rank, his carriages, food, clothing, and drink were all lustrous and lavish; he kept a dozen or more stable horses worth several hundred strings of cash each; at his grand banquets for guests he could not even name every dish; the headcloth he designed himself was so finely made that people competed to copy it, calling it the "Vice Minister's Cap."

sentences.zh: 領使既眾，吏白俸簿月二千緡，冕顧視，喜見顏間，世訾其嗜利云。

translations.literal: The commissions he held were many; a clerk reported that his salary ledger came to two thousand strings of cash per month; Mian looked it over and joy showed on his face—later ages reviled his love of profit.
translations.idiomatic: His concurrent commissions were numerous; when a clerk reported that his monthly salary ledger came to two thousand strings of cash, Mian looked it over with visible delight—later ages reviled his greed.

sentences.zh: 始，肅宗廟惟苗晉卿配享，冕卒後二十餘年，有蘇正元者奏言：「肅宗為元帥時，師才一旅，冕於草創中，甄大義以勸進，收募驍勇幾十餘萬。

translations.literal: At first in Emperor Suzong's temple only Miao Jinqing received joint sacrifice; more than twenty years after Mian's death a man named Su Zhengyuan memorialized saying: "When Emperor Suzong was commander-in-chief his army was but one brigade; Mian in the midst of founding enterprise discerned the great principle to urge advancement and gathered fierce warriors to nearly a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At first only Miao Jinqing received joint sacrifice in Emperor Suzong's temple; more than twenty years after Mian's death a man named Su Zhengyuan memorialized: "When Emperor Suzong was commander-in-chief his forces numbered but a single brigade; amid the founding struggle Mian discerned the great principle of urging him to take the throne and raised nearly a hundred thousand fierce warriors.

sentences.zh: 既逾月，房琯來；

translations.literal: After more than a month Fang Guan came;
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later Fang Guan arrived;

sentences.zh: 又一年，而晉卿至。

translations.literal: after another year Jinqing arrived.
translations.idiomatic: and a year after that Jinqing arrived.

sentences.zh: 今晉卿從祀，而冕乃不與。」

translations.literal: Now Jinqing follows in sacrifice, yet Mian is not included.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jinqing shares in sacrifice, yet Mian is excluded.

sentences.zh: 有詔冕配享肅宗廟。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Mian enshrined for joint sacrifice in Emperor Suzong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Mian granted joint sacrifice in Emperor Suzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 裴遵慶

translations.literal: Pei Zunqing
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zunqing

sentences.zh: 裴遵慶，字少良，絳州聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Zunqing, styled Shaoliang, was a native of Wenxi in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zunqing, styled Shaoliang, came from Wenxi in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼強學，該綜圖傳，外晦內明，不幹當世。

translations.literal: From youth he studied strenuously, mastered charts and chronicles comprehensively, was outwardly obscure yet inwardly bright, and did not meddle with the age.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied strenuously and mastered charts and chronicles; outwardly retiring yet inwardly sharp, he kept aloof from worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 年既長，始以仕家推蔭為興寧陵丞，調大理丞。

translations.literal: When his years had grown long he first entered office through yin privilege as an official household and was appointed deputy of Xingning Mausoleum, then transferred to aide in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Only when he was older did he enter office through yin privilege as deputy of Xingning Mausoleum, then transfer to aide in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 邊將蕭克濟督役苛暴，役者有醜言，有司以大逆論，遵慶曰：「財不足聚人，力不足加眾，焉能反？」

translations.literal: The frontier general Xiao Keji supervised labor with harsh cruelty; laborers had ugly words; the authorities judged it great treason; Zunqing said: "Without wealth one cannot gather men; without strength one cannot overcome the multitude—how could they rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: The frontier general Xiao Keji supervised corvée labor with harsh cruelty; the laborers spoke rebelliously, and the authorities charged them with high treason; Zunqing said, "Without wealth one cannot gather followers, and without strength one cannot overcome the multitude—how could they rebel?"

sentences.zh: 由是全救數十族。

translations.literal: Thereby he fully saved several tens of clans.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he saved several dozen entire clans.

sentences.zh: 頻擢吏部員外郎，判南曹。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Outer Director in the Ministry of Personnel and judged the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to outer director in the Ministry of Personnel and assigned to judge the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 天寶時，選者歲萬計，遵慶性強敏，視簿牒，詳而不苛，世稱吏事第一。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era candidates each year ran to ten thousand; Zunqing's nature was forceful and keen; viewing ledgers he was thorough yet not harsh—the age called him first in clerical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era annual selections ran to ten thousand candidates; forceful and keen by nature, Zunqing reviewed ledgers with thoroughness but without harshness—the age ranked him first in personnel administration.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In Emperor Suzong's time he was Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Suzong he served as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 蕭華輔政，屢薦之，拜黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Xiao Hua assisted in government he repeatedly recommended him; Zunqing was appointed Vice Director of the Gate and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Hua held power he repeatedly recommended him; Zunqing was appointed vice director of the gate and grand councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 代宗初，仆固懷恩反，帝以遵慶忠厚大臣，故奉詔宣慰，懷恩聽命將入朝，既而為其將范志誠沮止。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Daizong's reign Pugu Huai'en rebelled; the Emperor, because Zunqing was a loyal and sincere great minister, ordered him to go as imperial emissary to console; Huai'en obeyed and was about to enter court, but was then stopped by his general Fan Zhicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Daizong's reign Pugu Huai'en rebelled; the emperor, deeming Zunqing a loyal and sincere senior minister, sent him with an edict to console the rebels; Huai'en agreed to submit and was about to enter court, but was then blocked by his general Fan Zhicheng.

sentences.zh: 時帝在陜，遵慶脫身赴行在。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then at Shan; Zunqing escaped his body and hastened to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Shan; Zunqing escaped and hastened to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 帝還，遷太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned, Zunqing was moved to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Zunqing was promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 罷為集賢院待制，改吏部尚書，以尚書右僕射復知選事，朝廷優其老，聽就第註官，時以為榮。

translations.literal: He was dismissed to awaiting-orders scholar at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, changed to Minister of Personnel, and as Minister of the Right again handled selection affairs; the court favored his age and permitted him to register appointments at his residence—contemporaries regarded this as honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed to awaiting-orders scholar at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then made minister of personnel; as minister of the right he again handled selections; the court favored his age and permitted him to register appointments from home—contemporaries regarded this as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 嘗有族子病狂易，告以謀反，帝識其謬，置不問。

translations.literal: Once a clansman by marriage, sick with mania, reported that Zunqing was plotting rebellion; the Emperor recognized the absurdity and set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Once a clansman by marriage, deranged by illness, accused him of plotting rebellion; the emperor recognized the absurdity and took no notice.

sentences.zh: 性惇正，老而彌謹。

translations.literal: By nature he was sincere and upright; in old age he became all the more cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Sincere and upright by nature, he grew only more cautious in old age.

sentences.zh: 每薦賢，有來謝者，以為恥。

translations.literal: Whenever he recommended the worthy, if any came to thank him he regarded it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he recommended talent, he felt ashamed if anyone came to thank him.

sentences.zh: 諫而見從，即內益畏。

translations.literal: When he remonstrated and was heeded, inwardly he grew all the more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When he remonstrated and was heeded, he grew only more inwardly fearful.

sentences.zh: 雖親近，但記其削稿疏數，而莫知所言。

translations.literal: Even those close to him only noted how many draft memorials he cut, and did not know what he said.
translations.idiomatic: Even those close to him knew only how many draft memorials he submitted, not what they contained.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年薨，年九十餘。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dali he died at more than ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Dali at more than ninety.

sentences.zh: 初為郎時，著《王政記》，述今古治體，識者知其有公輔器云。

translations.literal: When he first served as a gentleman he wrote "Records of Royal Government," narrating the governing structures of past and present; those who knew him recognized that he had the capacity of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When he first served as a court gentleman he wrote "Records of Royal Government," surveying the governing structures of past and present; those who knew him recognized the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 子向。

translations.literal: His son was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 向字傃仁，以蔭得調。

translations.literal: Xiang, styled Siren, entered office through yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, styled Siren, entered office through yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 建中初，李紓為同州刺史，奏署判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong Li Shu was prefect of Tongzhou and memorialized that he be entered on staff as aide.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era Li Shu, as prefect of Tongzhou, had him entered on staff as aide.

sentences.zh: 李懷光叛河中，使其將趙貴先築壘於同州，紓奔奉天，而向領州務。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong and sent his general Zhao Guixian to build ramparts at Tongzhou; Shu fled to Fengtian while Xiang took charge of the prefecture's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong he sent his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tongzhou; Shu fled to Fengtian while Xiang took charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貴先脅吏督役，不及期，將斬以徇，民皆駭散，向獨詣貴先壘開諭之，貴先乃降。

translations.literal: Guixian coerced clerks to supervise labor; when the deadline was not met he was about to behead someone as warning; the people were all terrified and scattered; Xiang alone went to Guixian's camp to open persuasion, and Guixian then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guixian coerced clerks to drive the labor; when the deadline was missed he was about to behead a man as warning, and the people fled in terror; Xiang alone went to Guixian's camp and persuaded him, and Guixian then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 同州不陷，向力也。

translations.literal: That Tongzhou did not fall was Xiang's doing.
translations.idiomatic: That Tongzhou did not fall was Xiang's doing.

sentences.zh: 累為櫟陽、渭南令，奏課皆第一，擢戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Liyang and Weinan; in all memorial reports of performance he ranked first and was promoted to Outer Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as magistrate of Liyang and Weinan; in every performance report he ranked first and was promoted to outer director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 德宗末，方鎮之副，多自選於朝，以待有變，次授之，故向以選為太原少尹、行軍司馬，歷陜虢觀察使，以吏部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Dezong's reign deputies of frontier commands were mostly chosen from the court to await change and then assigned in turn; thus Xiang through selection became junior prefect of Taiyuan and campaigning chief military administrator, passed through Regional Inspector of Shan-Guo, and retired as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Dezong's reign deputies for frontier commands were often chosen from the capital to await emergencies and then assigned in turn; Xiang was thus selected as junior prefect of Taiyuan and campaigning chief military administrator, later served as regional inspector of Shan-Guo, and retired as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 向能以學行持門戶，內外親屬百餘口，祿俸必均，世稱其孝睦。

translations.literal: Xiang was able to uphold the household through learning and conduct; inner and outer kin numbered more than a hundred mouths, and salary and stipend were always divided equally—the age praised his filial piety and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang upheld his household through learning and conduct; more than a hundred kin within and without the family shared salaries and stipends equally—the age praised his filial devotion and harmony.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died at eighty and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty and was posthumously made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 子寅，官累御史大夫。

translations.literal: His son Yin successively reached Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin rose to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 寅子樞。

translations.literal: Yin's son was Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son was Shu.

sentences.zh: 樞字紀聖，咸通中，第進士。

translations.literal: Shu, styled Jisheng, in the Xiantong era passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, styled Jisheng, passed the jinshi examination in the Xiantong era.

sentences.zh: 杜審權鎮河中，奏署幕府，再遷藍田尉。

translations.literal: When Du Shenquan held Hedong he memorialized that Shu enter his staff; he was twice promoted to magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Shenquan governed Hedong he had Shu entered on his staff; Shu was twice promoted to magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 宰相王鐸知之，遂直弘文館。

translations.literal: Chancellor Wang Duo knew of him and had him appointed directly to the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Duo took notice of him and had him appointed directly to the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 鐸罷，樞久不調。

translations.literal: When Duo was dismissed Shu went long without reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo left office Shu went long without reassignment.

sentences.zh: 從僖宗入蜀，擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xizong into Shu and was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xizong into Shu and was promoted to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 中和初，鐸為都統，表署鄭滑掌書記。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe Duo was supreme commander and entered him on staff as secretary of Zheng-Hua.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhonghe era Duo served as supreme commander and had him entered on staff as secretary for Zheng-Hua.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，進給事中，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was advanced to Supervising Censor and changed to Prefect of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longji era he was advanced to supervising censor and made prefect of the capital.

sentences.zh: 與孔緯厚善，緯以罪貶，故樞改右庶子，出為歙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was thick friends with Kong Wei; when Wei was demoted for crime Shu was changed to Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent and sent out as prefect of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with Kong Wei; when Wei was demoted for a crime Shu was made right subordinate of the heir apparent and sent out as prefect of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 遷右散騎常侍，為汴州宣諭使。

translations.literal: He was moved to Right Regular Attendant and made imperial emissary to console Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right regular attendant and made imperial emissary to console Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 樞素與朱全忠相結納，故全忠聽命，修貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: Shu had long been bound in alliance with Zhu Quanzhong; therefore Quanzhong obeyed orders and tribute and offerings never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had long been allied with Zhu Quanzhong; Quanzhong therefore obeyed his orders and kept tribute flowing without interruption.

sentences.zh: 昭宗悅，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was pleased and promoted him to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong was pleased and promoted him to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時崔胤亦倚全忠專朝柄，因與樞善。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Yin also relied on Quanzhong to monopolize court power and therefore was on good terms with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cui Yin also relied on Quanzhong to monopolize court power and therefore befriended Shu.

sentences.zh: 俄以戶部侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made vice minister of revenue and grand councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 帝在鳳翔，貶胤官，樞亦罷為工部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was at Fengxiang Yin was demoted in office and Shu was also dismissed to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Fengxiang Yin was demoted and Shu was also removed to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 已還宮，拜檢校尚書右仆射、同平章事。

translations.literal: After returning to the palace he was appointed acting Minister of the Right and Concurrent Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to the palace Shu was appointed acting minister of the right and concurrent councillor.

sentences.zh: 出為清海節度使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as military commissioner of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military commissioner of Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 全忠言樞有經世才，不宜棄外，復拜門下侍郎平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: Quanzhong said Shu had talent to order the age and should not be abandoned outside; he was again appointed Vice Director of the Gate, Councillor, and supervisor of compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong said Shu had talent to govern the age and should not be cast out; Shu was again appointed vice director of the gate, councillor, and supervisor of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 累進右僕射、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: He was successively advanced to Minister of the Right and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport in all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively advanced to minister of the right and commissioner for salt and iron transport in all circuits.

sentences.zh: 哀帝嗣位，柳璨方用事，全忠以牙將張廷範為太常卿，樞以為廷範勛臣，自宜任方鎮，何用為卿，恐非王意，持不下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aidi succeeded, Liu Can was just then in power; Quanzhong wished to make his military officer Zhang Tingfan Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Shu held that Tingfan was a meritorious minister and ought to be assigned to a frontier command—what use was there in making him director? He feared this was not the king's intent and withheld the appointment without issuing it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aidi succeeded, Liu Can was in power; Quanzhong wished to make his military officer Zhang Tingfan director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Shu held that as a meritorious minister Tingfan ought to hold a frontier command—what use was there in making him court director? He feared this was not the king's intent and withheld the appointment.

sentences.zh: 全忠怒謂賓佐曰：「吾常器樞不浮薄，今乃爾。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong angrily told his guests and aides: "I always valued Shu as not shallow and frivolous—now he is like this."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong angrily told his staff: "I always thought Shu was not shallow and frivolous—now look at him."

sentences.zh: 璨聞，即罷樞政事，拜左僕射。

translations.literal: When Can heard, he immediately removed Shu from state affairs and appointed him Minister of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: When Can heard, he immediately removed Shu from state affairs and appointed him minister of the left.

sentences.zh: 俄貶登州刺史，又貶瀧州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was demoted to prefect of Dengzhou and again demoted to aide in the Ministry of Revenue at Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted to prefect of Dengzhou, then again to revenue aide at Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 至滑州，全忠遣人殺之白馬驛，投屍於河，年六十五。

translations.literal: When he reached Huazhou Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post Station and cast his body into the river; he was sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Huazhou Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post Station and cast his body into the river; he was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 初，全忠佐吏李振曰：「此等自謂清流，宜投諸訶，永為濁流。」

translations.literal: At first Quanzhong's aide Li Zhen said: "These men call themselves the clear stream—they ought to be cast into the He, to be the muddy stream forever."
translations.idiomatic: At first Quanzhong's aide Li Zhen said, "These men call themselves the pure stream—they ought to be thrown into the Yellow River and become the muddy stream forever."

sentences.zh: 全忠笑而許之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong laughed and assented.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong laughed and agreed.

sentences.zh: 呂諲，河中河東人。

translations.literal: Lü Yin was a man of Hedong in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yin came from Hedong in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少力於學，志行整飭。

translations.literal: From youth he strove in study; his aims and conduct were orderly and disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he strove in study; his aims and conduct were orderly and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 孤貧不自業，裏人程氏財雄於鄉，以女妻諲，亦以諲才不久困，厚分貲贍濟所欲，故稱譽日廣。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor, he could not support himself; a villager of the Cheng clan was wealthy and powerful in the district; he gave his daughter to Yin in marriage and also, because Yin's talent would not long remain in hardship, generously divided property to supply what he desired—hence praise spread day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he could not support himself; a wealthy Cheng clansman in the district gave him his daughter in marriage and, believing Yin's talent would not long remain in hardship, generously supplied his needs—hence his reputation spread.

sentences.zh: 開元末，入京師，第進士，調寧陵尉，采訪使韋陟署為支使。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan he entered the capital, passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Ningling, and Regional Inspector Wei Zhi entered him on staff as branch commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he entered the capital, passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Ningling, and was entered on the staff of regional inspector Wei Zhi as branch commissioner.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰節度河西，表支度判官。

translations.literal: When Geshu Han was military commissioner of Hexi he memorialized him as aide for branch supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When Geshu Han governed Hexi he memorialized Yin as aide for branch supplies.

sentences.zh: 歷太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: He passed through the post of Communications Aide of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as communications aide of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 性靜慎，勤總吏職，諸僚或出遊，諲獨頹然據案，鉤視簿最，翰益親之。

translations.literal: By nature he was quiet and cautious, diligent in summing clerical duties; when fellow officials went out on pleasure trips Yin alone sat collapsed over the desk, hooking through ledgers; Han grew all the more intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and cautious by nature, he was diligent in clerical duties; when fellow officials went out on pleasure trips Yin alone sat bent over his desk scrutinizing ledgers; Han grew all the more fond of him.

sentences.zh: 累兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He cumulatively served concurrently as Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He cumulatively served as palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 翰敗潼關，諲西趨靈武，由中人尉薦，肅宗才之，拜御史中丞，所陳事無不順納。

translations.literal: When Han was defeated at Tong Pass Yin hurried west to Lingwu; through recommendation by the eunuch Wei Jian, Emperor Suzong valued his talent and appointed him Vice Censor-in-Chief; whatever he presented was without exception accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Han was defeated at Tong Pass Yin hurried west to Lingwu; recommended by the eunuch Wei Jian, Emperor Suzong valued his talent and appointed him vice censor-in-chief; whatever he proposed was accepted.

sentences.zh: 從至鳳翔，遷武部侍郎。

translations.literal: He followed on to Fengxiang and was moved to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor to Fengxiang and was promoted to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 帝復兩京，詔盡系群臣之汙賊者，以御史中丞崔器、憲部侍郎韓擇木、大理卿嚴向為三司使處其罪，又詔御史大夫李峴及諲領使。

translations.literal: When the Emperor recovered the two capitals an edict ordered all ministers who had been stained as traitors imprisoned; Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi, Vice Minister of Justice Han Zemu, and Chief Justice Yan Xiang were made the Three Offices commissioners to dispose their crimes; another edict ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Xian and Yin to lead the commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor recovered the two capitals an edict ordered all officials who had served the rebels imprisoned; vice censor-in-chief Cui Qi, vice minister of justice Han Zemu, and chief justice Yan Xiang were made commissioners of the Three Offices to judge their crimes; another edict ordered censor-in-chief Li Xian and Yin to lead the commission.

sentences.zh: 諲於權宜知大體不及峴，而援律傅經過之，當時憚其持法，然以峴故，多所平反。

translations.literal: Yin in expedient grasp of the great principles did not equal Xian, yet in applying law and attaching classics he went too far; the age feared his upholding of law, yet because of Xian many cases were reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was inferior to Xian in grasping expedient principles, yet in applying law and citing classics he went too far; contemporaries feared his rigor, yet because of Xian many sentences were reversed.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，九節度兵敗，帝憂之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan the armies of nine military commissioners were defeated; the Emperor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyuan the armies of nine military commissioners were defeated, and the emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 擢諲同中書門下平章事，知門下省，翌日，復以李峴、李揆、第五琦為宰相，而苗晉卿、王玙罷。

translations.literal: Yin was promoted to Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery and put in charge of the Gate Department; the next day Li Xian, Li Kui, and Diwu Qi were again made chancellors, while Miao Jinqing and Wang Yu were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was promoted to grand councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery and put in charge of the gate department; the next day Li Xian, Li Kui, and Diwu Qi were again made chancellors while Miao Jinqing and Wang Yu were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 會母喪解，三月復召知門下省事，兼判度支，還執政。

translations.literal: He met his mother's mourning and was released; after three months he was again summoned to handle gate department affairs, concurrently judged the Department of Revenue, and returned to power.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office for mourning; after three months he was recalled to handle gate department affairs, concurrently judge the Department of Revenue, and return to power.

sentences.zh: 累封須昌縣伯，遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively enfeoffed as Earl of Xuchang and moved to Vice Director of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was cumulatively enfeoffed as Earl of Xuchang and promoted to vice director of the gate.

sentences.zh: 上元初，加同中書門下三品，當賜門戟，或勸諲以兇服受吉賜不宜，諲釋缞拜賜，人譏其失禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan he was given the third rank concurrent with the Secretariat and Chancellery; when court halberds were to be bestowed some urged Yin that in mourning garb to receive an auspicious gift was improper; Yin removed his hemp and bowed to receive the gift—people ridiculed his breach of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era he was given third rank concurrent with the Secretariat and Chancellery; when court halberds were to be bestowed some urged that receiving an auspicious gift in mourning garb was improper; Yin removed his hemp mourning dress and bowed to receive the gift—people ridiculed his breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 諲引妻之父楚賓為衛尉少卿，楚賓子震為郎官。

translations.literal: Yin brought in his wife's father Chu Bin as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia; Bin's son Zhen served as a court gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yin brought in his wife's father Chu Bin as vice director of the Court of Imperial Regalia; Bin's son Zhen served as a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 中人馬尚言者，素匿於諲，為人求官，諲奏為藍田尉。

translations.literal: The eunuch Ma Shangyan had long been hidden with Yin; he sought office for others; Yin memorialized that he be made magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Ma Shangyan had long been sheltered by Yin; he sought offices for others, and Yin memorialized that he be made magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 事覺，帝怒，命敬羽窮治，殺尚言，以其肉賜從官，罷諲為太子賓客。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed the Emperor was angry, ordered Jing Yu to investigate to the end, killed Shangyan, gave his flesh to attending officials, and dismissed Yin to Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed the emperor was furious, ordered Jing Yu to investigate thoroughly, executed Shangyan, gave his flesh to attending officials, and dismissed Yin to guest of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 數月，拜荊州長史、澧朗峽忠等五州節度使。

translations.literal: After several months he was appointed Chief Administrator of Jingzhou and military commissioner of the five prefectures Li, Lang, Xia, Zhong, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was appointed chief administrator of Jingzhou and military commissioner of the five prefectures Li, Lang, Xia, Zhong, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 諲始建請荊州置南都，詔可。

translations.literal: Yin was the first to propose establishing a southern capital at Jingzhou; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was the first to propose establishing a southern capital at Jingzhou; an edict approved.

sentences.zh: 於是更號江陵府，以諲為尹，置永平軍萬人，遏吳、蜀之沖，以湖南之嶽、潭、郴、道、邵、連，黔中之涪凡七州，隸其道。

translations.literal: Thereupon the name was changed to Jiangling Prefecture; Yin was made prefect; the Ever-Peace Army of ten thousand men was established to block the thrust between Wu and Shu; the seven prefectures Yue, Tan, Chen, Dao, Shao, Lian of Hunan and Fu of Qianzhong were all placed under his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The district was renamed Jiangling Prefecture with Yin as prefect; the Ever-Peace Army of ten thousand men was established to block the route between Wu and Shu; the seven prefectures Yue, Tan, Chen, Dao, Shao, and Lian in Hunan and Fu in Qianzhong were placed under his circuit.

sentences.zh: 初，荊州長史張惟一以衡州蠻酋陳希昂為司馬，督家兵千人自防，惟一親將牟遂金與相忤，希昂率兵至惟一所捕之，惟一懼，斬其首以謝，悉以遂金兵屬之，乃退，自是政一出希昂，後入朝，遷常州刺史，過江陵入謁，諲伏甲擊殺之，誅黨偶數十人，積屍府門，內外震服。

translations.literal: At first Chief Administrator Zhang Weiyi of Jingzhou made the Man chieftain of Hengzhou Chen Xi'ang his military administrator, supervising a thousand household troops for self-defense; Weiyi's intimate general Mou Suijin quarreled with him; Xi'ang led troops to Weiyi's place to seize him; Weiyi was afraid, beheaded Suijin's head to apologize, and turned over all Suijin's troops to him, then withdrew; from this government issued entirely from Xi'ang; later he entered court and was moved to prefect of Changzhou; passing Jiangling he entered to pay respects; Yin set hidden soldiers and struck him dead, executed several tens of his party by pairs, piled corpses at the prefectural gate—inside and outside were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: At first chief administrator Zhang Weiyi of Jingzhou made the Man chieftain of Hengzhou Chen Xi'ang his military administrator with a thousand household troops for self-defense; Weiyi's intimate general Mou Suijin quarreled with him; Xi'ang led troops to seize Suijin at Weiyi's residence; frightened, Weiyi beheaded Suijin to apologize and turned all his troops over to Xi'ang, who then withdrew; thereafter government issued entirely from Xi'ang; later Xi'ang entered court and was made prefect of Changzhou; passing Jiangling he came to pay respects; Yin set ambush soldiers and killed him, executed several dozen of his followers in pairs, and piled corpses at the prefectural gate—inside and outside were awed into submission.

sentences.zh: 妖人申泰芝用左道事李輔國，擢諫議大夫，置軍邵、道二州間，以泰芝總之，納群蠻金，賞以緋紫，出褚中詔書賜衣示之，群蠻怵於賞，而財不足，更為剽掠，吏不敢制。

translations.literal: The sorcerer Shen Taizhi used heterodox ways to serve Li Fuguo and was promoted to Remonstrance Councillor; an army was placed between Shao and Dao prefectures with Taizhi in overall command; he collected gold from the various Man, rewarded them with crimson and purple, produced imperial edicts from his sleeve to bestow robes and show them; the Man were cowed by rewards yet their wealth was insufficient and they turned again to plunder—officials did not dare restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer Shen Taizhi used heterodox arts to serve Li Fuguo and was promoted to remonstrance councillor; troops were placed between Shao and Dao with Taizhi in overall command; he collected gold from the Man tribes, rewarded them with crimson and purple robes, and produced edicts from his sleeve to bestow imperial garments; cowed by rewards yet lacking funds, the Man turned again to plunder—and officials dared not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 潭州刺史龐承鼎疾其奸，因泰芝過潭，縛付吏，劾贓鉅萬，得左道讖記，並奏之。

translations.literal: Tanzhou Prefect Pang Chengding hated his wickedness; when Taizhi passed through Tan he bound him and handed him to officials, impeached him for bribes of tens of thousands, obtained heterodox prognostic texts, and memorialized all together.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhou prefect Pang Chengding hated his wickedness; when Taizhi passed through Tan he bound him and handed him to the authorities, impeached him for bribes in the tens of thousands, obtained heterodox prognostic texts, and memorialized the whole case.

sentences.zh: 輔國矯追泰芝還京，既召見，反譖承鼎陷不辜，詔諲按罪。

translations.literal: Fuguo forged an order recalling Taizhi to the capital; after he was summoned and received, he in turn slandered Chengding for framing the innocent; an edict ordered Yin to investigate the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo forged an order recalling Taizhi to the capital; after an audience Taizhi slandered Chengding for framing the innocent; an edict ordered Yin to investigate.

sentences.zh: 諲使判官嚴郢具獄，暴泰芝惡。

translations.literal: Yin sent his aide Yan Ying to complete the case file and expose Taizhi's evil.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent his aide Yan Ying to complete the case file and expose Taizhi's crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝不省，賜承鼎死，流郢建州。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not understand; he granted Chengding death and exiled Ying to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen; he sentenced Chengding to death and exiled Ying to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 後泰芝終以贓徙死，承鼎追原其誣。

translations.literal: Later Taizhi ultimately died in exile for bribery; Chengding was posthumously cleared of the false charge.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizhi ultimately died in exile for bribery; Chengding was posthumously cleared of the false charge.

sentences.zh: 諲為治，不急細務，決大事剛果不撓。

translations.literal: In governing, Yin did not press small affairs; in deciding great matters he was firm and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: In governing Yin did not fuss over small matters; in deciding great affairs he was firm and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 始在河西，悉知諸將能否，及為尹，奏取材者數十人總牙兵，故威惠兩行。

translations.literal: When he was first in Hexi he fully knew which generals could or could not; when he became prefect he memorialized that several tens of able men be gathered to command the guard troops—hence awe and favor both prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first in Hexi he knew every general's strengths and weaknesses; as prefect he memorialized that several dozen able men command the guard troops—hence both awe and favor prevailed.

sentences.zh: 諲之相，與李揆不平，既斥，乃用善治聞。

translations.literal: When Yin was chancellor he was on bad terms with Li Kui; after he was dismissed he became known for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor Yin was on bad terms with Li Kui; after his dismissal he became known for good governance.

sentences.zh: 揆恐帝復用，即妄奏置軍湖南非便，又陰遣人刺諲過失。

translations.literal: Kui feared the Emperor would reuse him and immediately memorialized falsely that establishing an army in Hunan was inconvenient; he also secretly sent men to probe Yin's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Kui feared the emperor would recall him and falsely memorialized that establishing an army in Hunan was inadvisable; he also secretly sent men to probe Yin's faults.

sentences.zh: 諲上疏訟其事，帝怒，逐揆出之，顯條其罪。

translations.literal: Yin submitted a memorial pleading the matter; the Emperor was angry, drove Kui out, and openly listed his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yin submitted a memorial pleading his case; the emperor was angry, drove Kui out, and openly listed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 諲苦羸疾，卒，年五十一，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Yin suffered from emaciating illness and died at fifty-one; he was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Yin suffered from wasting illness and died at fifty-one; he was posthumously made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 諲在朝不稱任職相，及為荊州，號令明，賦斂均一。

translations.literal: At court Yin did not fit the office of chancellor; when he became prefect of Jingzhou his orders were clear and levies uniform.
translations.idiomatic: At court Yin was not regarded as fit for the chancellorship; as prefect of Jingzhou his orders were clear and his levies even-handed.

sentences.zh: 其治尚威信，故軍士用命，闔境無盜賊，民歌詠之。

translations.literal: His governance valued prestige and trust; therefore soldiers obeyed orders, the whole circuit had no bandits or thieves, and the people sang praises of him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule rested on prestige and trust; soldiers obeyed without question, bandits vanished from the circuit, and the people sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 自至德以來，處方面數十人，諲最有名。

translations.literal: From Zhide onward several tens of men held frontier commands; Yin was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhide era onward dozens of men held frontier commands, but none was more renowned than Yin.

sentences.zh: 荊人生構房祠，及歿，吏裒錢十萬徙祠府西。

translations.literal: The people of Jing built a shrine to him of their own accord; when he died officials collected a hundred thousand in cash and moved the shrine west of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jing built a shrine to him of their own accord; when he died officials collected a hundred thousand strings of cash and moved the shrine west of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 始，諲知杜鴻漸、元載才，薦於朝，後皆為宰相。

translations.literal: At first Yin recognized the talent of Du Hongjian and Yuan Zai and recommended them to court; both later became chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Yin early recognized the talent of Du Hongjian and Yuan Zai and recommended them to court; both later became chancellors.

sentences.zh: 永泰中，嚴郢以故吏請謚有司，博士獨孤及謚曰「肅」，郢以故事宰相謚皆二名，請益曰「忠肅」。

translations.literal: In Yongtai Yan Ying as a former subordinate requested a posthumous title from the authorities; Academician Dugu Ji gave the title "Su"; Ying, citing precedent that chancellors' posthumous titles were all two characters, requested addition to make "Zhongsu."
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongtai era Yan Ying, as a former subordinate, requested a posthumous title from the authorities; academician Dugu Ji proposed "Su"; Ying, citing precedent that chancellors' posthumous titles always had two characters, asked that it be expanded to "Zhongsu."

sentences.zh: 及執奏，謂：「謚在義美惡，不在多名。

translations.literal: When he presented the memorial he said: "Posthumous titles lie in praising good and condemning evil, not in many names.
translations.idiomatic: When he presented the memorial he said, "Posthumous titles praise good and condemn evil—they do not depend on many characters.

sentences.zh: 文王伐崇，周公殺三監、淮夷，重耳一戰而霸，而謚曰文。

translations.literal: King Wen attacked Chong; the Duke of Zhou killed the Three Overseers and the Huaiyi; Chong'er became hegemon after one battle—yet their posthumous titles were "Wen."
translations.idiomatic: King Wen attacked Chong; the Duke of Zhou killed the Three Overseers and the Huaiyi; Chong'er became hegemon after a single battle—yet their posthumous titles were "Wen."

sentences.zh: 冀缺之恪，寧俞之忠，隨會不忘其君，而謚曰武。

translations.literal: Ji Que's reverence, Ning Yu's loyalty, Sui Hui's not forgetting his lord—yet their posthumous titles were "Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Que's reverence, Ning Yu's loyalty, Sui Hui's faithfulness to his lord—yet their posthumous titles were "Wu."

sentences.zh: 故知稱其大、略其細也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that titles praise the great and pass over the small.
translations.idiomatic: Thus titles praise what is great and pass over what is small.

sentences.zh: 且二名謚，非古也。

translations.literal: Moreover two-character posthumous titles are not ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover two-character posthumous titles are not ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 漢興，蕭何、張良、霍去病、霍光以文武大略，佐漢致太平，一名不盡其善，乃有文終、文成、景桓、宣成之謚。

translations.literal: When Han rose, Xiao He, Zhang Liang, Huo Qubing, and Huo Guang—with civil and military grand strategies assisted Han to reach great peace—one character could not exhaust their excellence; hence there were the posthumous titles Wenzong, Wencheng, Jinghuan, and Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose, Xiao He, Zhang Liang, Huo Qubing, and Huo Guang—with grand civil and military strategies—helped Han to peace; one character could not exhaust their excellence, hence the posthumous titles Wenzong, Wencheng, Jinghuan, and Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 唐興，參用漢制，魏徵以王道佐時近『文』，愛君忘身近『貞』，二者並優，廢一莫可，故曰文貞。
