translations.literal: When Tang rose it adopted Han institutions; Wei Zheng in assisting the age with the kingly way was close to "Wen," in loving the lord and forgetting self close to "Zhen"—both excellences together, abandoning one was impossible—hence he was called Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang rose it adopted Han institutions; Wei Zheng's kingly assistance to the age approached "Wen," his love of the lord and forgetfulness of self approached "Zhen"—both excellences together, neither could be dropped—hence he was called Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀端直近『貞』，性多猜近『褊』，言『褊』則失『貞』，稱『貞』則遺『褊』，故曰貞褊。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu's uprightness was close to "Zhen," his nature much suspicious close to "Pian"—to say "Pian" loses "Zhen," to call "Zhen" omits "Pian"—hence he was called Zhenpian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu's uprightness approached "Zhen," his suspicious nature approached "Pian"—to say "Pian" loses "Zhen," to say "Zhen" omits "Pian"—hence he was called Zhenpian.

sentences.zh: 蓋有為為之也。

translations.literal: These were all done with deliberate purpose.
translations.idiomatic: These were all deliberate exceptions.

sentences.zh: 若跡無異稱，則易以一字。

translations.literal: If the record had no special designation, then a single character would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Where the record offered no special distinction, a single character would suffice.

sentences.zh: 故杜如晦曰成，封德彜曰明，王珪曰懿，陳叔達曰忠，溫彥博曰恭，岑文本曰憲，韋世源曰昭，皆當時赫赫居宰相位者，謚不過一名。

translations.literal: Thus Du Ruhui was called Cheng, Feng Deyi Ming, Wang Gui Yi, Chen Shuda Zhong, Wen Yanbo Gong, Cen Wende Xian, Wei Shiyuan Zhao—all at the time illustrious in chancellor posts, their posthumous titles no more than one character.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Du Ruhui was posthumously Cheng, Feng Deyi Ming, Wang Gui Yi, Chen Shuda Zhong, Wen Yanbo Gong, Cen Wende Xian, Wei Shiyuan Zhao—all illustrious chancellors of their day, each with no more than one posthumous character.

sentences.zh: 而言故事宰相必以二名，固所未聞。

translations.literal: Yet to say that by precedent chancellors must have two names is something never heard of.
translations.idiomatic: To claim that by precedent chancellors must have two-character titles is something never heard of.

sentences.zh: 宜如前謚。」

translations.literal: The former posthumous title should stand."
translations.idiomatic: The earlier posthumous title should stand."

sentences.zh: 遂不改。

translations.literal: It was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: It was not changed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：孔子稱才難。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Confucius called talent hard to find.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Confucius declared that talent is hard to find.

sentences.zh: 然人之才有限，不得皆善。

translations.literal: Yet human talent has limits and cannot all be good.
translations.idiomatic: Yet human talent has its limits—not everyone can excel in everything.

sentences.zh: 觀圓之銳，而失守出奔；

translations.literal: Consider Yuan's keenness, yet he lost his post and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yuan's keen ambition, yet he lost his post and fled;

sentences.zh: 晉卿雅厚，而少風采臧否；

translations.literal: Jinqing's elegant generosity, yet little spirit in judging others' rights and wrongs;
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing's elegant generosity, yet little force in judging others;

sentences.zh: 冕明強，嗜利不知大體；

translations.literal: Mian's clarity and strength, yet love of profit without knowing the great principles;
translations.idiomatic: Mian's clarity and strength, yet greed without grasp of the larger principles;

sentences.zh: 諲輔政，功名不及治郡。

translations.literal: Yin's assisting government—merit and fame did not equal governing a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's service as chancellor—his merit and fame did not match his record as a regional governor.

sentences.zh: 然各以所長顯於時。

translations.literal: Yet each displayed at the time what he excelled in.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each made his strengths known in his own time.

sentences.zh: 故聖人使人也器之，不窮所不能而後為治也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage in employing men treats them as vessels, not exhausting what they cannot do and only then governing.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage employs men according to their capacities, not demanding what they cannot give—and only then achieves good government.

sentences.zh: 遵慶寡疵，中人之賢與。

translations.literal: Zunqing had few flaws—the worth of an average man, was it not?
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing had few flaws—he was the worth of an average good man.
